# @zakkster/lite-map

> Zero-GC keyed list reconciliation for @zakkster/lite-signal: mapArray and
> indexArray that MOVE and REBIND per-item reactive scopes instead of rebuilding
> them, reusing retired scopes from a free-list so steady-state list churn never
> grows the engine pool.

Map a reactive array to one reactive scope per item. List mutation moves and
rebinds scopes; only changed items recompute. The differentiator vs Solid's
mapArray: removed items' scopes go to a free-list and are REUSED by later
inserts, so churn over a bounded set pulls nothing from the pool.

Peer dependency: @zakkster/lite-signal ^1.6.0-preview.0 (uses createScope, the
detached per-item-subtree disposal primitive). ESM only. DOM-free. MIT.

## The fork this ships

By-accessor: the CHANGING dimension is always an accessor. That is what lets a
retired scope be reused for a new item by setting its signals (no rebuild). This
is the zero-GC default. [1.3] A by-value mapArray (item as a plain value) ships as
an explicit opt-in: `mapArray(list, mapFn, { byValue: true })` -- a MOVE stays
pool-flat (idxSig.set, no mapFn re-run) but an INSERT re-runs mapFn and pulls a
fixed node count from the pool, because a by-value view bakes the item and cannot
be redirected. See the [1.3] section.

## Entry points

- createMapper(reg) -> { mapArray, indexArray }   // bind to any registry >=1.6.0-preview.0
- mapArray(list, mapFn, opts?)                     // default registry, item-keyed
- indexArray(list, mapFn, opts?)                   // default registry, position-keyed

## indexArray(list, (item, index) => O, { maxPool? })

- POSITION-keyed. `item` is an accessor (the value at this slot); `index` is a
  plain number (the slot is stable).
- Value churn at a stable length = itemSig.set per changed slot. Zero-GC.
- Grow appends; shrink parks tail slots to a LIFO free-pool; tail re-grow reuses a
  parked slot when its index matches (push/pop at the end is zero-GC). A reused
  slot whose index would not match is disposed + rebuilt (keeps the plain `index`
  correct). maxPool caps retained parked slots.

## mapArray(list, (item, index) => O, { key?, maxPool? })

- ITEM-keyed. BOTH `item` and `index` are accessors.
- key: identity selector, default reference identity (the item). Keys must be
  unique within the list: only the FIRST occurrence of a key is addressable, so a
  duplicate gets its own scope but is unreachable by key. [1.1] A duplicate is
  contained -- it is not registered in byKey, so it cannot evict the owner's entry;
  a transient duplicate no longer costs a unique key its scope once unique again.
- Survivor reused in place; if it moved, idxSig.set (zero-GC); if its item changed
  under a stable key, itemSig.set. Removed -> retired to the free-list. New -> a
  retired scope reused via itemSig.set + idxSig.set (zero-GC when the pool is
  warm), else built. maxPool caps retained retired scopes.
- TAIL FAST-PATHS [1.1]: a position-aligned common-prefix scan by key classifies
  append / pop / same-order value-churn BEFORE the general keyed diff. When the
  prefix is intact, byKey / scratch swap / full retire scan are skipped -- only
  O(delta) tail work runs (Map + scope pool never churn). Non-tail shapes
  (prepend, reorder, middle insert/remove) fall through to the general path.
  Correctness-preserving: identical results to the general diff. No API change.

## Returned accessor: Mapped<O>

- mapped() -> O[]   the outputs in source order. ONE persistent array, mutated in
  place (zero per-change allocation): read fresh each run; do not retain or
  reference-compare. Fires only on a real structural change (membership/order),
  not on value-only churn.
- mapped.dispose()   stop the driver, dispose every live + parked scope (including
  the item/index signals the scope does not own) and the output signal.
- mapped.stats() -> { live, parked, highWater }   [1.2] pool counters, BOTH
  primitives. live = current slot count (= mapped().length); parked = free-list
  length; highWater = all-time peak of (live + parked). Historical: survives
  dispose(), which pins { 0, 0, <peak> } (no throw).

## mapped.stats() [1.2]

- Pool observability for a mapped list: a read surface for a monitor, for tuning
  maxPool by measurement, or for a scoped counter (vs the whole engine ledger).
- ONE Object.freeze'd object per list, REUSED on every call: allocation-free per
  read (getters read the current slot/pool lengths + a closure high-water counter).
  stats() === stats() (reference-stable); Object.keys is [live, parked, highWater].
- LIVE VIEW: the three fields change between reads WITHOUT another stats() call, so
  destructure/snapshot if you need a point-in-time copy. Same discipline as the
  persistent mapped() output array.
- highWater is the all-time peak of (live + parked) -- exactly the mark the "growth
  past the previous high-water allocates" non-claim is about, now measurable: a run
  stays pool-flat while live + parked never exceeds it. A replace-all (n old + n new
  keys in one set) genuinely coexists both generations, so highWater records the
  prevN + n transient, not the settled count.
- maxPool: 0 is falsy and is treated as UNSET (unbounded) today -- pass >= 1 to
  bound the pool. Documented, not changed.

## Ownership

- Each item owns a createScope() scope; its mapFn effects/computeds are cascaded
  on disposal. Per-item scopes AND the reconcile driver are detached from the
  caller (createRoot/createScope), so an enclosing scope re-running never tears
  the list down. The caller owns teardown via mapped.dispose() -- there is no
  auto-cleanup.

## Zero-GC (engine pool counters), and the honest non-claims

PASS (poolGrowths / totalAllocations flat after warm-up, verified):
- indexArray value churn at a stable length (20k updates flat).
- mapArray reorder/move (idxSig.set on shifted survivors).
- mapArray warm-pool insert/remove churn (5k iters flat).
- indexArray tail grow/shrink via the free-pool.
- mapArray tail append/pop/value-churn [1.1]: 10k push/pop cycles on a warm list
  flat; append to an N-list preserves all N survivor scopes (prefix scan is
  O(min(n,prevN)) comparisons, but allocation/Map/scope-move cost stays flat).
NOT claimed:
- Growth past the previous high-water mark pulls scopes from the pool.
- The keyed byKey Map mutates (set/delete) on actual key changes -- a JS
  allocation the pool counters do not see. Reorder touches no key, so no Map churn.
- The user's mapFn body (its allocations are the caller's).

## Gotchas

- createScope cascades effects/computeds but NOT signals (the engine never
  owner-adopts signals). lite-map disposes the item/index signals it creates. A
  BARE signal you create inside mapFn is NOT auto-disposed on scope teardown --
  prefer effects/computeds (which ARE cascaded), or dispose it yourself.
- Call mapArray/indexArray once at setup; reading the returned accessor is the
  reactive surface. Disposal is explicit (mapped.dispose()).
- Deferred to a later minor: LIS minimal-move ordering (1.0 moves are correct but
  not minimal). Append/pop tail fast-paths shipped in 1.1; by-value mapArray
  shipped in 1.3 (see the [1.3] section).

## by-value mapArray [1.3]

- Opt in with `mapArray(list, mapFn, { byValue: true })`. mapFn is called
  `(item, index) => O` -- `item` is the PLAIN value (Solid-style), `index` is an
  accessor. The by-accessor mode (byValue absent/false) is the zero-GC default and
  is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Cost, stated at the call site: a MOVE (same item, new index) rides idxSig.set
  with NO mapFn re-run -- reorders stay pool-flat. An INSERT re-runs mapFn exactly
  once and pulls a fixed node count k from the pool (a by-value view bakes the item
  in its closure -- there is no signal to redirect, so a parked scope cannot serve
  a new item). Gated: the T6 phase-4 window pins k == 3 engine nodes/insert for the
  1-effect fixture and 0 pool growth on a warm reorder.
- Keys are the item by REFERENCE identity (SameValueZero): -0 and 0 are the same
  key (not an item change); the same reference twice is a contained duplicate.
- No free-list: removals dispose IMMEDIATELY, so `stats().parked` is always 0.
- Door (fail closed, ASCII did-you-mean): `byValue + key`, `byValue + maxPool`, and
  a truthy-non-true `byValue` each throw at creation.
